subject: a vertical phone photograph looking south down the Hudson River at dusk from a wooded hillside: a broad flat river filling the middle of the frame, steep dark green mountain shoulders closing in from the left and right, a low wooded island in the middle distance carrying the ruined brick shell of Bannerman Castle, further ridgelines receding in layers toward a hazy gap on the horizon, an overcast sky of soft grey and lilac cloud bands with faint pink catching the undersides, and a dense mass of green sumac fronds and broadleaf branches filling the bottom third of the frame in the near foreground
keep: Keep the exact same composition, camera position, framing, vertical orientation and horizon line. Keep every element exactly where it is and the same shape and size: the castle ruin on its island, the shoreline, the near and far ridgelines, the gap on the horizon, and every branch and frond in the foreground mass. Do not add, remove, move or redesign any structure, boat, island or landmass. Do not add people, birds or aircraft. Do not crop, zoom, straighten or re-frame. This is a colour, light and atmosphere pass on a real photograph, not a reimagining.

looks.natural_color: Do a clean, restrained colour edit that brings out what is already in the frame rather than adding anything new. Recover the pink and lilac that is genuinely in the cloud bands and let it read clearly instead of washing out. Bring back the true green in the foreground foliage and the blue-green in the mountain slopes, which are currently crushed dark and flat. Add the faint warm note on the castle brick. Lift the haze off the river so it holds its soft silver reflection with real tonal separation from the far shore. Modest global contrast, gentle clarity, correct the slight blue-grey cast toward neutral. This should look like a careful raw develop of this exact frame that someone made ten minutes after taking it: believable, natural, nothing pushed. No heavy saturation, no HDR, no glow.
looks.golden_sunrise: Regrade to a warm break in the overcast just after sunrise. Let low warm light come through the gap on the horizon and rake up the river, amber and rose firing along the undersides of the cloud bands, a warm specular path on the water leading the eye to the island, and the castle brick catching the warmest light in the frame. Keep the foreground foliage in cool green shade so it reads as a silhouette layer against the lit water. Rich, film-like, natural.
looks.moody_bluehour: Regrade to deep blue hour twenty minutes after the sun has gone. Indigo and slate across the sky with the last cold magenta bleeding along the cloud edges, the river dark, glassy and near-monochrome, the ridgelines flattened into layered silhouettes, and a few small warm lights showing on the far shore and in the castle ruin. Moody, high contrast, quiet, cinematic.
looks.autumn_fog: Regrade to a still autumn morning with low fog sitting on the river. Ochre, rust and amber running through the hillsides and the foreground foliage, soft diffused light, and fog banks separating the foreground mass, the island, the mid ridges and the far horizon into clearly distinct depth layers. Muted, painterly, quiet.
looks.bw_fine_art: Convert to a fine-art black and white landscape in the large-format tradition. Deep controlled blacks in the foreground foliage, luminous separation in the cloud bands, the river rendered as a smooth silver sheet, and the receding ridgelines held apart by tonal value alone rather than colour. Strong midtone structure, fine silver-halide grain, no crushed shadows and no blown highlights. Think a printed exhibition frame, not a desaturated colour file.
